reply.text:
You can train fine without a plan built around skipping carbs, but I'd be honest with you: carbs are the fuel for harder lifting and faster running, so cutting them out entirely usually makes hard sessions feel flat and recovery slower. Easy walks, light cycling and technique-focused lifting are doable on low fuel, but heavy or high-volume work is where you'll notice it most.

I'd rather work on the fear itself. Carbs don't make you gain fat on their own, and most people train better with some around their sessions. If it's tied to weight or how you eat in general, a doctor or dietitian is the right person to talk it through with, and I'll happily build the training side around whatever they land on.

If you'd like, tell me how many days a week you can train and what you want out of it, and I'll set up a program.
